engagement_background.objective: Choice Health engaged Treya Partners to capture $0.54–$1.2 million in annual savings through strategic sourcing, leverage enterprise-wide purchasing power across key indirect and clinical spend areas, and establish a best-in-class procurement process by July 2024.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project initially targets 12 spend categories (Fleet, Employee Benefits, Medical Supplies, Pharmacy, Medical Equipment, Temp Labor – Therapists & Nurses, Telecom – Data & Voice, Commercial Print, Copiers/MFPs, Office Supplies, IT Hardware) representing about $17.7 million in annual spend and 80-90 % addressability. Other categories (e.g., Homecare Software, Assisted Living, DME) are out of scope unless mutually added later.
constraints_challenges: Supplier lack of responsiveness to data and usage requests
Potential supplier push-back and need for a unified client/Treya communication front
Risk of uncontrolled ‘side conversations’ between internal users and suppliers during negotiations
Limited stakeholder bandwidth to provide timely data, feedback, and approvals
Pressure to demonstrate quick wins within a six-month timeline driven by PE value-creation goals
Inconsistent or incomplete historical usage data, requiring supplier outreach and data cleansing

procurement_environment.data_availability: High-level AP spend file was available; detailed line-item usage data and current contracts had to be requested from suppliers and various internal sources.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Vendor names required deduping and GL mapping; significant gaps in usage history for several suppliers; no centralized contract repository.
